chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has farms, some of which are close to each other, so he goes out and tours them; does he complete the prayer or shorten it? He said, 'He completes it.'

And what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and others from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who goes out to his farm and stays for one day, two days, or three days; does he shorten or complete? He said, 'He completes the prayer whenever he visits a farm from his farms.'

So there is nothing in these two narrations that contradicts what we mentioned earlier, because they do not specify the distance he travels, and if that is not specified in them, it is possible that the meaning is when the farm is close to him, so it is not obligatory for him at that time to shorten.
ai.seo_question: Does a traveler visiting nearby farms need to shorten their prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the boundary between travel (*safar*) and local movement by distinguishing between visiting distant lands versus nearby agricultural plots (*diya'*). The Imams rule that if the farms are close together or near the residence, the traveler completes (*tamm*) his prayers, as the short distance does not trigger the legal status of a journey requiring *qasr*. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly principle that the physical distance, rather than the purpose of the trip, determines the obligation of shortening prayer.
